fossil
The papersThe code

PROSPECTR disease-gene ranking, dug back up.

35 results: 0 exact, 6 agree, 15 partly agree, 1 inconclusive, 6 differ, 7 not attempted. PROSPECTR's Perl scorer is lost, but its training and test sets survive in the Wayback Machine. Run on them, the paper's own tree gives Table 3's training accuracy (67.2% against 67%) and Fig. 3A's curve.

Fig. 2

Fig. 2. PROSPECTR's 15-rule alternating decision tree. Ours: the tree Weka 3.4.3 builds with the download page's recipe on the archived training set, as Weka prints it.

Partly agrees
Fig. 2, the 15-rule alternating decision tree
5 of 59 values, Partly agrees

Retrained on the archived training set, the recipe puts rules on mouse identity, signal peptide, gene length and exon number at the root, as Figure 2 does, with other thresholds and values (exons > 31 against > 32); the other 11 rules differ. The archived sets are not the paper's: the PROSPECTR site's ARFFs, first captured on 2006-09-30, hold 1,080 + 1,080, 713 + 713 and 50 + 50 genes (the paper: 1,084 + 1,084, 675 + 675 and 54 + 54) and 64 features from a later Ensembl build (Table 1 lists 23), with no gene IDs.

Fig. 3

Fig. 3. ROC curves of the classifier on the training set (A), the HGMD test set (B) and the oligogenic test set (C). Ours: the published tree on the archived sets, drawn as Weka draws them.

Inconclusive
Fig. 3A, ROC curve, training set (the published tree on the archived set)
92.6% within 2 px, Agrees
Fig. 3B, ROC curve, HGMD test set (the published tree on the archived set)
52.5% within 2 px, Inconclusive
Fig. 3C, ROC curve, oligogenic test set (the published tree on the archived set)
62.4% within 2 px, Partly agrees

The pixel score cannot confirm this panel: ours scores 0.52 and two controls score higher (the retrained tree 0.62, ours shifted by +0.02 in FP rate 0.61). Only the AUC agrees (0.693 against Table 3's 0.69; the published points read back give 0.692). The archived HGMD set has 713 + 713 genes, the paper's 675 + 675. Same shape and hull; the points sit on another grid because the archived oligogenic set has 50 + 50 genes (steps of 2%), the paper's 54 + 54 (1.85%). AUC 0.767 against Table 3's 0.76 (the published points read back give 0.770).

Mouse identity is 22.9% (21%) and paralog identity 0% (2%): the archived paralog identities are all 0, so rule 7 never fires.
Text: 10- and 20-rule trees perform worse than 15 (cross-validated, retrained)Partly agrees3 of 4 values
  • 10 rules: lower cross-validated accuracy than 15: paper yes, ours no
  • 10 rules: lower cross-validated AUC than 15: paper yes, ours yes
  • 20 rules: lower cross-validated accuracy than 15: paper yes, ours yes
  • 20 rules: lower cross-validated AUC than 15: paper yes, ours yes
On the archived training set the 20-rule tree is worse than 15 on accuracy and AUC, and the 10-rule tree worse on AUC but not on accuracy (67.0% against 66.6%). The paper gives no numbers ('details not shown').
Text: a 15-rule tree on gene and protein length alone (69% found, 51% misclassified)Differs0 of 2 values
  • disease genes found, training set (%): paper 69, ours 83.7037
  • controls called disease, training set (%): paper 51, ours 58.1481
Retrained on gene_length and residue_length of the archived training set, the tree finds 84% of disease genes and calls 58% of controls disease, against 69% and 51%: it puts the threshold elsewhere. Accuracy is 62.8% against the paper's (69 + 49) / 2 = 59%.
Text: comparison with Lopez-Bigas and Ouzounis on 260 HGMD genes (72% against 47%; kappa 0.282 against 0.158)Not attemptedThe 260 genes were not published and the archived HGMD set has no gene IDs.
Fig. 4 and the artificial-loci numbers (HGMD, OMIM and POCUS targets in 30 Mb loci)Not attemptedNeeds the target genes' IDs, every gene's position and every gene's score; the archived sets have no IDs and the genome-wide dump is a later model. Fig. 4 is read back to check the text's numbers against it (text.arithmetic).
Text: substitutions, gross lesions and micro-lesions (75%, 54%, 77%)Not attemptedNeeds HGMD's mutation records for the test genes; HGMD needs registration, its 2003 release is not public and the archived set has no gene IDs.
Text: genome-wide scores (97 genes over 0.75, 4,357 under 0.3, ~44% called disease), from the authors' dump.tabDiffers0 of 4 values
  • genes scoring over 0.75: paper 97, ours 2
  • genes scoring under 0.3: paper 4,357, ours 5155
  • Additional File 1 genes that score over 0.75 in dump.tab: paper 61, ours 0
  • share of the genome called disease (%): paper 44, ours 42.05
The authors' own genome-wide dump (captured 2005-04-27) has 2 genes over 0.75 and 5,155 under 0.3, and none of Additional File 1's genes over 0.75: it comes from another model than Figure 2. Its raw scores reach 3.25, more than the Figure 2 tree can give (3.015).
Additional File 1, the 61 top-scoring genes not known in diseaseNot attemptedScoring every Ensembl gene with the published tree needs every gene's features from EnsMart 22.1 and HomoloGene, which were not archived (the Ensembl 22 mart folder is empty); the archived dump is another model. The file's own numbers are checked in text.arithmetic and text.normalisation.
Text: the normalisation 1/(1 + γ^α), 'γ = Euler's constant'AgreesThe scores follow 1/(1 + e^α): 'Euler's constant' is Euler's number e, not the Euler-Mascheroni constant γ.
Claims recomputed from the paper's own numbers and figuresAgreesMost claims follow from the paper's own numbers and figures. Slips: 36 of 97 is 37%, not ~33%; 29 of 219 is 13.2%, not 13.4%; the abstract's 'twenty-fold 11% of the time' is the conclusion's 25-fold (Fig. 4 at the top 4% reads 11.0%, at the top 5% 12.4%); and the kappas of the Lopez-Bigas comparison (0.282, 0.158) do not follow from the rates the text gives (0.287, 0.163). The abstract's five-fold 37% reads 38.6% off Fig. 4, just outside the 1.5-point reading margin.
Port of Weka 3.4's ADTree (prospectr_adtree) against Weka 3.4.3Agrees
Weka 3.4.1, 3.4.2 and 3.4.4 against 3.4.3 on the download page's recipeAgrees
Python package prospectr_adtree and its tutorialAgrees

The main claim holds on the surviving data: the published tree separates disease genes from controls about as well as Table 3 says (training accuracy 67.2% against 67%; HGMD 63.0% against 64.5%; oligogenic 67% against 65%). The differences come from the archived sets, which are a later version of the paper's; six of 58 claims in the paper's own arithmetic do not follow (text.arithmetic).

PROSPECTR's tree as the Python package prospectr_adtree.

What stayed buried

  • The paper's own gene lists: the archived ARFFs carry no gene IDs and hold 1,080, 713 and 50 disease genes, not 1,084, 675 and 54.
  • Fig. 4 and the artificial loci, the Lopez-Bigas comparison and the mutation types: they need gene IDs, HGMD records or positions that were never published.
  • Additional File 1 and the genome-wide numbers: the archived score dump comes from another model, and EnsMart 22.1 was not archived.

The main claim holds on the surviving data: the published tree separates disease genes from controls about as well as Table 3 says (training accuracy 67.2% against 67%; HGMD 63.0% against 64.5%; oligogenic 67% against 65%). The differences come from the archived sets, which are a later version of the paper's; six of 58 claims in the paper's own arithmetic do not follow (text.arithmetic).

What we matched

How each part of the paper's method was rebuilt.

Classifier
Weka 3.4.3's ADTree, -B 15 -E -1, the command on PROSPECTR's archived download page.
Scorer
Figure 2's 15 rules; unknown features skip their rules; a negative score means disease-like.
Normalisation
1/(1 + e^score); the paper's 'Euler's constant' is e.
Statistics
Accuracy, precision, recall, AUC and kappa as Weka 3.4.3 computes them, 10-fold folds as the Explorer draws them.
Data
PROSPECTR's own training and test ARFFs, captured by the Wayback Machine in 2006.

PROSPECTR's tree came back from its figure, and its data from the Wayback Machine.
